question: For the four-member binary-reward policy and local clipped-GRPO score update in the preceding exact witness, what order of within-group clean-label marginals is sufficient and necessary to identify the expected update under arbitrary conditional reward laws?
selection_disclosure: This follow-up was motivated by the already-published four-member exact witness and exploratory exact truth-table calculations. It is a deterministic characterization of a fixed finite estimand, not a preregistered empirical confirmation or independent novelty claim.
scope: Exact finite mathematics and CPU enumeration only. No model training, stochastic simulation, capability metric, or audit algorithm.

policy_and_estimand.action_distribution: independent Bernoulli(1/4) actions; all 16 action vectors have positive probability
policy_and_estimand.reward_domain: all binary reward vectors in {0,1}^4; conditional reward law may be any distribution for each observed action vector
policy_and_estimand.update: G(a,y)=sum_i A_i(y)*(a_i-1/4), where A is population-standardized binary group reward and is zero for a constant-reward group
policy_and_estimand.clipped_objective: At the old policy, ratio=1 is in the interior of epsilon=0.2 clipping, so G is the local derivative of the maximized surrogate

audit_observation_model.selection: Subset-selection probabilities may depend on a and public randomization but not on unobserved clean labels
audit_observation_model.order_k: Across groups and action strata with positive policy probability, the audit design identifies the conditional joint marginal law of y_S for every S with |S|<=k; each required action/subset stratum has positive audit probability

theorem_to_verify.claim: For a fixed action vector a with positive probability, E[G(a,Y)|a] is identified by all conditional label marginals of order at most k for every possible conditional reward law if and only if every Walsh-Fourier coefficient of f_a(y)=G(a,y) on {0,1}^4 with support size greater than k is zero.
theorem_to_verify.basis: chi_T(y)=product_{i in T}(1-2*y_i)=(-1)^(sum_{i in T} y_i); alpha_T(a)=2^-4*sum_y f_a(y)*chi_T(y)
theorem_to_verify.sufficiency: The Walsh expansion contains only terms indexed by sets of size at most k, and each such expectation is determined by a corresponding observed joint marginal.
theorem_to_verify.necessity: If alpha_T(a)!=0 for |T|>k, the distributions P_+(y)=2^-4*(1+epsilon*chi_T(y)) and P_-(y)=2^-4*(1-epsilon*chi_T(y)), 0<epsilon<=1, are valid, agree on every marginal of order at most k, but have expected f_a values differing by 2*epsilon*alpha_T(a).

frozen_checks: exactly enumerate all 16 action vectors and 16 reward vectors per vector
derive every Walsh coefficient with exact rational-plus-sqrt(3) arithmetic
verify all coefficients of order four vanish
verify every nonconstant action vector has at least one nonzero coefficient of order three
verify constant action vectors have identically zero update
for target action 0001 and T={0,1,2}, verify alpha_T=-3/8+sqrt(3)/4 is nonzero
construct P_plus/P_minus at epsilon=1/2 and verify exact equality of all one- and two-coordinate marginals
verify the conditional expected-update gap equals 2*epsilon*alpha_T and the unconditional gap equals the action probability times that gap
verify each order-three marginal observation differs while all order-at-most-two observations agree
interpretation_limits: The theorem is a finite Boolean-function identification criterion, not a new general RL algorithm.
The degree-three result applies only to this four-member binary-reward local score update and stated standardization convention.
No claim is made about prevalence, practical audit cost, finite-sample estimator variance, trained policies, verifier drift, or task capability.
Related work on group-correlated verifier noise, GRPO advantage behavior, selective auditing and adaptive verification is close; novelty is unresolved.
